title: Antiparticles, neutrinos and beta energy spectra

questions.prompt: For beta-plus emission, state the nucleon number and charge of the emitted beta particle.
Which statement relates an electron to a positron?

options.A: They have equal mass and equal charge.
options.B: They have equal mass and opposite charge.
options.C: They have opposite mass and equal charge.
options.D: They have opposite mass and opposite charge.

questions.prompt: Which additional particle is emitted during beta-minus decay?
Which description matches the measured kinetic energies of alpha and beta particles from fixed nuclear transitions?

options.B: Both occur only at discrete values.
options.C: Alpha energies are discrete and beta energies form a continuous range.
options.D: Alpha energies form a continuous range and beta energies are discrete.

questions.prompt: A diagram compares an electron with its antiparticle.

figure.purpose: Assess particle-antiparticle properties without revealing them in labels.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired comparison diagram with an electron box labelled charge -e and mass m, and a second blank particle box with blank charge and mass fields. Do not name the second particle or fill its properties.
figure.alt_text: An electron is compared with an unnamed antiparticle whose charge and mass fields are blank.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Name the antiparticle of the electron.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State its charge and its mass in terms of m.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State the additional particle emitted with it during beta-plus decay.

questions.prompt: A beta-minus decay has 3.20 MeV available to the electron and electron antineutrino. In one event the electron has kinetic energy 1.25 MeV. Ignore nuclear recoil for this model.

figure.purpose: Assess energy sharing and connect repeated events to a continuous beta spectrum.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired energy-sharing diagram. Show a 3.20 MeV total bar, one electron branch labelled 1.25 MeV and one blank antineutrino branch. Beside it show blank axes for number detected against beta kinetic energy. Do not draw the spectrum curve.
figure.alt_text: A beta decay shares 3.20 MeV between an electron and antineutrino beside blank spectrum axes.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why many such decays produce a continuous range of electron kinetic energies even though each event conserves energy.

questions.prompt: A laboratory produces a short-lived nuclide ^{30}_{15}X which undergoes beta-plus decay to nuclide Y. The total kinetic energy available to the emitted positron, electron neutrino and recoiling Y is 2.84 MeV. In one event the positron has 1.06 MeV and Y has 0.08 MeV.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use conservation of nucleon number and charge to determine A and Z for Y.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy carried by the neutral particle in this event.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain why positrons from many identical decays are measured with a continuous range of kinetic energies.
